---
title: "Refresh a session without rewriting the sessions array"
description: "Drop when the pinned release refreshes a session without writing back the sessions array it read."
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm upstream export` from the patch's commit message on top of Payload v4.0.0-beta.2. Edit the commit, not this page. -->

Refreshing a token while another request logs in or refreshes as the same
user fails or loses sessions. Refresh reads the user with its sessions, then
writes the whole user back with the new expiry of its session and without
the expired sessions. The SQL adapters write an array by deleting all of its
rows and inserting them again. D1 has no transactions, so refreshes that run
at once interleave those statements and fail with "UNIQUE constraint failed:
users_sessions.id". On D1 and Postgres, a session that a login adds after a
refresh reads the user disappears when the refresh writes, and its token
stops working. Between the delete and the insert, a request with the
refreshing token finds no session. Refresh also writes back every other
field it read, which can undo a concurrent edit to the user.

Refresh now updates the expiry of its own session in place, then removes the
expired sessions it read by ID with the $remove operator that
concurrent-login-sessions adds. The session keeps its ID, and refresh writes
no other row. updateOne accepts { $update: row | row[] } on a top-level
array field, where each row has the ID of an existing row and the fields to
set. The SQL adapters update the columns of each row with one statement, and
MongoDB sets the fields through array filters. MongoDB with transactions
still rejects concurrent writes to one user with a WriteConflict, as before.

- **Patch:** `concurrent-session-refresh`, committed as `fix(payload): refresh a session without rewriting the sessions array`
- **Upstream:** Not proposed
- **Tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit packages/drizzle/src/upsertRow/updateArrayRows.spec.ts; PAYLOAD_DATABASE=sqlite pnpm test:int test/auth/int.spec.ts; e2e suite (sessions.spec.ts refresh test)`
